title: Display 3 decimal places by default for Volt, Watt, and Ampere sensor readings
line: System Monitor widgets now show voltage, power and current readings with three decimals, like 12.380 V instead of 12.4 V.
explanation: When a sensor face asks for no specific precision, libksysguard's formatter rounds every decimal value to one decimal, so a 0.869 V core voltage shows as 0.9 V and 13.439 W as 13.4 W, even though ksystemstats provides full precision from hwmon. The change keeps the existing rule for when decimals are shown at all, but uses three decimals instead of one when the displayed unit is plain V, W or A.

commits.message:
formatter: show volts, watts and amperes with three decimals

Decimal voltage, power and current readings were rounded to one decimal
by default, hiding the millivolt and milliwatt detail that hwmon gives.
Without an explicit precision, these base units now get three decimals.

BUG: 528611

patches.diff:
From a3d1fe07d9e5944344e92c40fe5f89ab6da6feae Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 13:47:57 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] formatter: show volts, watts and amperes with three decimals

Decimal voltage, power and current readings were rounded to one decimal
by default, hiding the millivolt and milliwatt detail that hwmon gives.
Without an explicit precision, these base units now get three decimals.

BUG: 528611
---
 formatter/Formatter.cpp | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/formatter/Formatter.cpp b/formatter/Formatter.cpp
index e42210be..8384578d 100644
--- a/formatter/Formatter.cpp
+++ b/formatter/Formatter.cpp
@@ -522,7 +522,7 @@ static QString formatNumber(const QVariant &value, Unit unit, MetricPrefix prefi
         if (value.typeId() == QMetaType::Double // If it's a double
             || adjusted > unit // or we're using a larger prefix
             || (value.typeId() == QMetaType::QString && value.toString().contains(QLocale().decimalPoint()))) { // or it's a string that contains a double
-            precision = 1; // use a higher precision
+            precision = (adjusted == UnitVolt || adjusted == UnitWatt || adjusted == UnitAmpere) ? 3 : 1; // use a higher precision
         } else {
             precision = 0; // else use a lower precision
         }
--
